Classify recent hybrids from microsatellites

Source: R/microsat.R
classify_hybrids_microsat.Rd

The multi-allelic version of classify_hybrids(): a parent with species-2 ancestry a passes on allele x with probability a * freq2(x) + (1 - a) * freq1(x). Each animal is tested against the pure, F1, F2, first- and second-backcross classes and against the best fit under any pair of parental ancestries; if no class fits (likelihood-ratio test at alpha), it is called "later".

Usage

classify_hybrids_microsat(alleles, ms, alpha = 0.01, error = 0.01)

Arguments

alleles

Allele matrix as in microsat_markers().

ms

Output of microsat_markers().

alpha

Significance level of the fit test. Many later-generation animals (for example backcrosses of backcrosses) have genotypes close to an early class and cannot be told apart one at a time. A larger alpha calls more of them "later" at the cost of rejecting some true early hybrids: in a bighorn sheep pedigree with 187 microsatellites, alpha = 0.01 kept 91% of early calls right and called 20% of later-generation sheep "later"; alpha = 0.1 gave 85% and 44%. Population ages from estimate_history() do not depend on this choice.

error

Probability that a called allele is replaced by a random allele of that locus (genotyping error, null alleles).

Value

A data.frame with class, probability and fit_p, one row per animal.

Examples

set.seed(1)
a <- cbind(L1.a1 = c(rep(100, 10), rep(104, 10)), L1.a2 = c(rep(100, 10), rep(104, 10)))
g <- rep(c("sp1", "sp2"), each = 10)
ms <- microsat_markers(a, g, "sp1", "sp2")
classify_hybrids_microsat(rbind(a, c(100, 104)), ms)
